rv.q: This is a very warmhearted show; a pick me up, you might say, or sing.
That turns out to be a sacrifice worth making.
I absolutely LOVE this musical. It creates a big community where all are eventually included and contains a dynamic message of hope.
This is an absolutely stellar addition to the pantheon of musical Shakespeare adaptations.
Writers Theatre's production...is crackling, sharp, and radiant.
There's no better message for Chicagoans to hear right now, and no better entertainment for them to see.

At Writers Theatre, there’s a breathtaking new musical production of AS YOU LIKE IT, cleverly adapted by two-time Tony Award-winner, Shaina Taub (SUFFS on Broadway) and Laurie Woolery, with music and lyrics that are based upon the Shakespearean text, also by Shaina Taub.
The tight cast is one of the great examples of ensemble acting this writer has seen in musical theatre in quite a while, as well as top-notch creators to represent.
Taub's songs are incredibly catchy and the performers are in top form.
The clothing diversity doesn't really work for me, as I wasn't sure what era we were visiting, which reinforces the disconnectedness I mentioned earlier.
But as an introduction to Shakespeare’s comedy, “As You Like It” has merit.

Nevertheless, this is an entertaining, big-hearted show, full of talent, with a lovely, fantastical set (Sara Ryung Clement and Jacelyn Stewart) featuring chandeliers hanging in the autumn-colored Arden trees.

cn.t: Critics praise this charming musical adaptation of Shakespeare's comedy, celebrating its folk-pop score, communal warmth, and top-notch ensemble performances that create a sparkling, foot-tapping delight for contemporary audiences.
